ideas.description: Move the resolution boundary later on the E040 tip (commit 18ce8ac: Muon NS3 batched, lr 0.16, mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for 1.5 epochs then 32 px for 5.25, 6.75 epochs total). Make one change: train at 24 px for the first 2.25 epochs and at 32 px for the last 4.5, keeping 6.75 epochs total, bs 1024 and the same step-indexed lr, Muon and lookahead schedules, which do not change because the total step count is unchanged. If the switch now falls mid-epoch, take the first part of that epoch's permutation at 24 px and the rest at 32 px, so the sample stream is unchanged. The whitening-bias freeze stays at the end of epoch 1. Before launching, check that every shape used in the timed path is warmed up in build(): 24 px with and without whitening-bias grad, 32 px without it, and any new partial-batch shape at the switch. Warm up with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout (E035 lesson). Run debug_nan.py on any new graph, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times. Risk to note: E040's 1.5 low-res epochs covered roughly the warmup phase (~23% of steps). This change pushes low-res into the peak-lr phase, where full-res steps may matter more.
ideas.expected: Time -3% to -6%, point -4.5% (~5.46 s vs 5.718 s): 0.75 epoch moves from ~0.87 s to ~0.53 s per epoch. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.1 pp, point -0.15 pp (~0.7544). E040 implies a 24 px epoch is worth ~0.83 of a full-res epoch, with some fall-off once low-res runs past warmup. Feasible means a new best. If it misses 0.753 by <=0.2 pp, the follow-up is 2.25 + 4.75 (7.0 total). A drop >=0.4 pp means low-res steps are only cheap during warmup; then fix the boundary at ~1.5 epochs and try the 28 px stage (H2.3.3) instead.

ideas.description: Add a middle 28 px stage to the E040 curriculum. On the E040 tip, make one change: 24 px for epochs 0-1.5 as now, then whole images bilinearly downsampled (antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip/translate) to 28 px for 1.5 epochs, then 32 px for the last 3.75 epochs. Total stays 6.75 epochs, bs 1024, step-indexed schedules unchanged. In drafts/, print the per-block spatial sizes at 28 px input first (expect whitening 27 -> pools 13/6/3). Set the 28 px graph's final pool to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to its final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (the E009 Inductor bug). Compile and warm up the 28 px train step without whitening-bias grad, plus any partial batch at the stage switches, in build() with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times to catch warmup gaps. Eval stays the 32 px graph.
ideas.expected: Time -3.5% to -7%, point -5% (~5.43 s): a 28 px epoch costs ~0.77x a 32 px epoch, and 1.5 full-res epochs move to 28 px. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.15 pp, point -0.12 pp (~0.7547). 28 px keeps more detail than 24 px, so each epoch should be worth ~0.9 of a full-res epoch. Feasible means a new best and supports H2.3.3's claim that the 28 -> 32 stage carries most of the saving. If both this and the 24 px boundary idea are feasible, the next step combines them (24 px to ~2 epochs, 28 px stage, 32 px ~3.5). A drop >=0.4 pp means late-ish full-res epochs are not replaceable; then refute H2.3.3 and close the multi-stage line.

ideas.description: On the E040 tip, double the head (final linear layer) lr in the SGD group. Keep lr*wd constant for the head by halving its wd. If the code expresses the head lr as a multiple of the group base lr, double that multiple; otherwise double the head param-group lr. The BN-bias lr x64, whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, the resolution curriculum and the epochs stay identical. This is a pure hyperparameter change: the lr is passed as a 0-d tensor, so there are no new shapes and nothing recompiles. Pre-registered follow-up to E039, where halving the head lr cost 0.41 pp on the then-tip.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.45 pp, point +0.12 pp (range 0.752-0.760 around tip 0.7559). Time unchanged within +-1.5% (~5.72 s). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.7.3 and banks ~0.2 epoch: next trim 0.25 epoch of 32 px training (~-3.8% time), and try head x3 as one run. A result within +-0.2 pp means the head lr sits at its optimum near 1x (E039 was the steep side); then close the head axis. A drop >=0.25 pp means 1x is the optimum from both sides.

ideas.description: On the E040 tip, change only the pre-NS normalization inside the batched compiled Muon step. Today each momentum matrix is scaled to Frobenius norm 1 before the 3 quintic NS iterations. Instead, scale it to Frobenius norm s_t, which decays linearly from 0.50 at step 0 to 0.08 at the final step (Hiverge's CIFAR-10 record). Pass s_t as a 0-d GPU tensor updated with fill_, so nothing recompiles. NS coefficients, the sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling, the weight-norm projection, Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead, curriculum and epochs stay unchanged. Run debug_nan.py on the Muon step under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. In drafts/, also log the mean update Frobenius norm per shape group at steps 0, 100 and end, so the effective-lr reduction is known when the result is read.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.6 to +0.35 pp, point -0.05 pp. Time unchanged (+-1.5%; one extra scalar multiply). This is an explore idea. The smaller, less-whitened late updates act partly like a lower Muon lr, which is untested below 0.16. A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.9.1 and banks margin for an epoch trim. A drop >=0.3 pp refutes it: full orthogonalization throughout is right at this horizon, and H1.9 closes. If the logged norms show late updates <0.5x the tip's, an accuracy change also bears on the untested low side of the Muon lr axis.

drop.reason: H1.4.1 has confidence 0.08 and its own point estimate (-0.9 pp for -13% time) is at break-even with the ~1.14 pp/epoch knee slope. On the E040 curriculum base it would need scoring and 512/424 train graphs for both the 24 px and 32 px stages, which multiplies the compile and warmup surface (E035-type leak risk) for a likely null-or-worse result. The 28 px stage and the boundary shift are cheaper ways to cut FLOPs per step, and E040 shows they work.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is now E040: a 24 px → 32 px bilinear curriculum, 5.718 s, accuracy 0.7559, margin 0.29 pp. It shows a low-res whole-image epoch is worth ~0.83 of a full-res epoch for ~61% of the time, making it the cheapest accuracy-per-time lever found on the Muon base.

**Two exploit ideas build on it, each with one change:**
- **Move the boundary later (H2.3.2, priority 4):** 2.25 epochs at 24 px then 4.5 at 32 px. Expected about -4.5% time and -0.15 pp accuracy. It also tests whether low-res steps stay cheap after warmup ends.
- **Add a 28 px middle stage (H2.3.3, priority 3):** 1.5 epochs at 24 px, 1.5 at 28 px, 3.75 at 32 px. Expected about -5% time and -0.12 pp.

**Two hyperparameter and update-geometry ideas:**
- **Head lr ×2 with wd halved (H1.7.3, priority 3):** the pre-registered follow-up to E039, where halving it cost 0.41 pp.
- **Hiverge-style pre-NS Frobenius scaling from 0.50 to 0.08 (H1.9.1, priority 2, explore).**

**Dropped I049** (selective backprop, H1.4.1). Its expected value is break-even, and on the curriculum base it would need many more compiled graphs.

**Kept as queued:**
- I043 (brightness/contrast jitter, H1.8.1)
- I047 (bs ramp, conditional on I042)
- I048 (BN-bias ×32, H1.7.1)
- I050 (bs 768, H1.2.3 probe)

These four were written against E034 and should be applied to the E040 curriculum tip, with every new batch shape warmed up at both the 24 px and 32 px resolutions.

**Not added:**
- NS2 with AOL (H2.4.5) and projection-frequency cuts (H2.4.3): the expected time cuts of about 1–1.2% are inside timing jitter. Keep them for a bundled systems change later.
- H1.6.6, H4.1.2, H4.1.4: these are offline diagnostics in drafts/, not scored experiments.

That leaves 8 queued ideas, with I042 (bs 1536) still running.
